newsitem.title: USA: Md. okays Baltimore school bill as deadline looms.
newsitem.headline: Md. okays Baltimore school bill as deadline looms.

text.p: The Maryland House of Delegates approved a plan to restructure the Baltimore City School system, providing an additional $254 million for schools in exchange for more state control.

The plan was approved by the House late Saturday night, but its version differs from the Senate-passed proposal. Conferees are set to work Monday on a compromise, as a midnight deadline looms for the end of the 1997 session.
Montgomery and Prince George's County legislators wanted to add more money for their school districts but were unsuccessful.
Lawmakers are also struggling to finish work on a final version of the fiscal 1998 budget.

Other issues on the legislative plate include a final vote on Gov. Parris Glendening's Smart Growth environmental plan. House and Senate conferees worked out a compromise over the weekend on a plan to funnel state money for development in areas where highways and utilities are already in place.
Supporters say it will relieve pressure on undeveloped areas of the state, keeping them green.
Conferees are also trying to find compromise language on the Thriving by Three health care plan to give free health care to needy children and pre-natal care for-low income women.
Glendening called both measures priorities, and said he is confident both will pass before tonight's midnight deadline.
